entries.title: The ten stems
entries.content: The ten heavenly stems are yang and yin pairs of each element: Gap/Eul (Wood), Byeong/Jeong (Fire), Mu/Gi (Earth), Gyeong/Sin (Metal) and Im/Gye (Water). Stems are read as the 'heaven' or outward layer of a chart.
entries.source: How to Read Marital Harmony (Gunghap 3) - Korea Times
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Stem combinations
entries.content: Some yang-yin stem pairs are said to 'combine', such as Gap Wood with Gi Earth. These pairs are read as natural affinity in a chart.
entries.source: How to Read Marital Harmony (Gunghap 3) - Korea Times
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Yang and yin stems
entries.content: Yang stems are read as active and outward, yin stems as receptive and steady. The calendar alternates between them.
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Gap Wood - yang wood
entries.content: Pictured as a tall tree with deep roots. Traditionally linked with ambition and principle, and sometimes stubbornness.
entries.source: Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia; The Five Elements (Ohaeng) in Korean Culture
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Eul Wood - yin wood
entries.content: Pictured as vines and flowers that bend and climb. Traditionally linked with gentleness, tact and resilience.
entries.source: Korea Times Gunghap 3; Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Byeong Fire - yang fire
entries.content: Pictured as the sun. Traditionally linked with warmth, openness and charisma, and sometimes impulsiveness.
entries.source: Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia; The Five Elements (Ohaeng) in Korean Culture
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Jeong Fire - yin fire
entries.content: Pictured as a candle or hearth flame. Traditionally linked with thoughtfulness, attention and refinement.
entries.source: Korea Times Gunghap 3; Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Mu Earth - yang earth
entries.content: Pictured as a mountain. Traditionally linked with steadiness, reliability and calm.
entries.source: Korea Times Gunghap 3; Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Gi Earth - yin earth
entries.content: Pictured as garden soil. Traditionally linked with patience, practicality and caring for others.
entries.source: Korea Times Gunghap 3; Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Gyeong Metal - yang metal
entries.content: Pictured as raw iron or a sword. Traditionally linked with courage, decisiveness and a strong sense of justice.
entries.source: Korea Times Gunghap 3; Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Sin Metal - yin metal
entries.content: Pictured as polished gold or jewelry. Traditionally linked with precision, taste and high standards.
entries.source: Korea Times Gunghap 3; Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Im Water - yang water
entries.content: Pictured as the ocean or a big river. Traditionally linked with resourcefulness and strategic thinking.
entries.source: Korea Times Gunghap 3; Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Gye Water - yin water
entries.content: Pictured as rain or morning dew. Traditionally linked with intuition, sensitivity and quiet wisdom.
entries.source: Korea Times Gunghap 3; Four Pillars of Destiny - Wikipedia
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection
